text:
dsh-history-fold README · dsh-history-fold：Every conversation that runs long enough hits the same wall: the history no longer fits, so
something has to be dropped. The built-in compactor drops it by *summarising*, and a summary of
eleven hours of work is not the parameter you needed, the path you saved, or the decision you
actually made. Ask about it two days later and you get a confident paraphrase of a memory nobody
kept.
section: dsh-history-fold

text:
dsh-history-fold README · dsh-history-fold：This plugin keeps the whole thing instead. The oldest span of history becomes **one message that
carries an extractive index** — real prefixes of the real messages, nothing paraphrased, no model
called — and every folded message is written **verbatim to a local archive first**. The visible
context gets short; the history does not disappear.

It is memory, not bookkeeping:
section: dsh-history-fold

text:
dsh-history-fold README · dsh-history-fold：- **Nothing is ever dropped without a copy on disk.** Archive first, fold second; if the write
  fails the fold is abandoned.
- **Nothing is summarised.** The lines in the index are the messages' own prefixes, so what the
  model sees is quoted evidence, not a rewrite.
- **The notes are regenerable from your session logs** — delete them entirely and the next refresh
  mines them back. Measured below.

text:
dsh-history-fold README · ⚠️ Read this first: precision is not the same as remembering：The engineering here is complete: lossless archive, recoverable index, semantic vectors,
extractive notes — each one real, each one tested. **None of that adds up to "it remembers what
you talked about."**

Measured against **659 human-labelled turns** out of this project's own 4,906-turn history:

| Metric | Measured |
|---|---|
| Turns that genuinely needed the archive, **correctly let through** | 51/87 = **59%** |
| Turns that did not need it, wrongly triggered | 43/572 = 7.5% |

text:
dsh-history-fold README · ⚠️ Read this first: precision is not the same as remembering：**Four times in ten, a turn that should have pulled up old context did not.** That is not a bug —
it is a deliberate trade:

| Configuration | Injections | Share of turns |

| 0.7 strict | 670 | 19.5% |
| 0.8, no classifier | 2,377 | 69.3% |
| **0.8 + classifier** (current) | 289 | **8.4%** |

**The saved tokens are real. So is what gets forgotten.**

dsh-history-fold README · 2026-10-29: the three real causes found and fixed：The 59% above is the classifier layer. Digging below it showed the missed recalls were mostly
**not** the classifier's fault. After fixing three things, measured end-to-end on 10 real questions:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| End-to-end recall (10 questions) | **3/10** | **9/10** |
| Chit-chat false positives (10 turns) | — | **1/10** (only "好的") |

The three causes:
section: 2026-10-29: the three real causes found and fixed

text:
dsh-history-fold README · 2026-10-29: the three real causes found and fixed：1. **`crossSession` defaulted to `false`** — only *this* session's notes were searched. Anything
   said in another session was outside the search radius entirely. **This was the biggest single
   cause.** Now on by default.
2. **`gateThreshold` defaulted to `0.50`, which sat inside a cluster** — "B65 到了怎么跑" scored
   0.444, "显存怎么分配" 0.424, "二班下好了吗" 0.413: all rejected by a hair. Lowered to 0.40,
   which recovers all of them at the cost of admitting one extra 闲聊 turn.
3. **`entity-map.json` coordinates were mostly broken** — bare filenames caused cross-session
   misalignment, line numbers ran past end-of-file or pointed at `##` headings, and keys shorter
   than 3 characters were skipped outright by `searchRare` (`桌宠`/`沙箱`/`肉鸽`/`双路`/`显存`
   had **never** fired). All 19 entries recomputed.

> not been re-run. Treat 9/10 as "what the new configuration does on these 10", not as "recall is

text:
dsh-history-fold README · 2026-10-29: the three real causes found and fixed：- **Inert by default.** A fresh install reads nothing, writes nothing and logs nothing
  until you configure it.
- **Lossless.** Every folded message is written to a local archive *before* the fold is
  committed, and the replacement tells the model exactly where to look.
- **No `node_modules` patching.** It uses the same public surface-replacement mechanism as
  the shipped compactor, so a DSH upgrade cannot break it.
- **Also works on DSH 0.2.x** (`0.2.0-rc.2`, `0.2.1-rc.2`), which changed four things this plugin
  depends on — two of which fail silently. See
  [DSH 0.2.x](#dsh-02x-0200-rc2--021-rc2--supported) for what changed and how each was measured.
- **Declares what it supports.** `engines.dsh` is set to `>=0.1.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`, so a loader that
  checks compatibility can tell you *before* mounting it rather than after it misbehaves.
- **The notes are regenerable.** Everything this plugin remembers is *derived* from your DSH session
  logs, not hand-maintained. Delete the entire notes directory and the next refresh mines it back out
  of the logs, byte for byte. Measured: one 1.7 MB session log → 25

The properties that made it shippable rather than merely interesting:
section: What's new in 0.8.0 — it learned when *not* to interrupt you

text:
dsh-history-fold README · What's new in 0.8.0 — it learned when *not* to interrupt you：- **1.3 MB, zero dependencies.** Plain JS over a JSON weight table: no ONNX, no runtime, no Python,
  no network call, no API cost. Inference is sub-millisecond; total recall overhead is 44–53 ms.
- **A filter, not an oracle.** It sits on top of the existing rules and can only *veto* them when it
  is confident a turn is noise. Explicit recall intent ("what did we decide last time…") never
  reaches it.
- **Missing model = unchanged behaviour.** If `model/gate-model.json` is absent or unreadable the
  layer is skipped and the rules decide exactly as in 0.7. Nothing is silently disabled, nothing
  silently enabled.
- **Trained on this project's own conversations**, not a public benchmark. That is also its limit —
  see [Limitations](#limitations).

text:
dsh-history-fold README · Why a summary is the wrong answer：Once that history is summarised, three things are gone permanently: the exact text, the ordering,
and the ability to check. You cannot `rg` a paraphrase. Ask "what did we set the threshold to, and
why" a week later and the honest answer is a plausible guess.
section: Why a summary is the wrong answer

text:
dsh-history-fold README · Why a summary is the wrong answer：This plugin takes the other option — **keep everything, shrink only the window**. Folded messages
are archived verbatim, so the answer to "what exactly did we say" is a file search away, and the
message that replaced them quotes real prefixes instead of inventing a narrative.
section: Why a summary is the wrong answer

text:
dsh-history-fold README · Why a summary is the wrong answer：That the request also gets shorter is a side effect, not the pitch: a shorter context is what keeps
a long conversation usable at all, and it is why the fold has to happen. What the plugin refuses to
do is make the fold *lossy*.

text:
dsh-history-fold README · What it does：Before a turn's first step, if the visible surface is above the trigger — `triggerRatio ×
contextWindow`, or an explicit absolute `triggerSurfaceTokens`, see
[how the thresholds are resolved](#how-the-two-thresholds-are-resolved) — the plugin:
section: What it does

text:
dsh-history-fold README · What it does：1. Picks the oldest run of nodes that ends on a tool-pairing **balanced** cut, leaves at
   least `keepRecentNodes` behind, and brings the surface down to about the target
   (`targetRatio × contextWindow`, default `0.14`).
2. **Archives** every folded node, verbatim, to
   `$DSH_HOME/history-fold/archive/<session>.jsonl`. If this write fails the fold is
   abandoned — history is never dropped without a copy on disk first.
3. Replaces that range with **one** `user/message`, using the same mechanism as the shipped
   compactor:
   ```js
   session.append('user/message', message, {
     surfaceOp: { op: 'replace', start, end },
     sourceEventSeqs: [/* every shadowed seq */],
   })
section: What it does

text:
dsh-history-fold README · What it does：`dsh-session` then splices the replacement into the old range's position, so chronology
   is preserved and the conversation still reads in order.
section: What it does

text:
dsh-history-fold README · What it does：**If that fold did not land, there is a second chance.** When the next turn still finds the
surface at or above `emergencyTriggerRatio` (0.8 of the window, 800k on a 1M window), the
normal attempt clearly did not bring it down — `keepRecentNodes` covered the whole foldable
span, the `minFold*` floors refused a small fold, or an archive write failed and the fold was
abandoned. The plugin then retries with the recent window cut back to
`emergencyKeepRecentNodes` (12) and the floors lowered to `emergencyMinFoldNodes` /
`emergencyMinFoldTokens`. It is the same bounded fold: the same archival of every node, the
same refusal to split a tool-call/tool-result pair. It just stops being polite about how much
history it holds back — and every line of that fold carries `emergency: true` in the log, so a
reader can tell the two paths apart afterwards.
section: What it does

text:
dsh-history-fold README · The replacement is an index, not a summary：The message that enters the context window is a **notice plus an extractive index** — every
sampled line is the real prefix of that message's own text. **No model is called**, and
nothing is paraphrased:

```
[dsh-history-fold] 614 earlier messages (surface seqs 223995..387899) were folded out of the
visible history so this session stays fast.
NOTHING WAS DELETED. Their full text is archived at:
  /…/.dsh/history-fold/archive/session-….jsonl
section: The replacement is an index, not a summary

text:
dsh-history-fold README · The replacement is an index, not a summary：If the index would exceed `digestMaxChars` it samples every *n*-th line rather than
truncating, and says so.
section: The replacement is an index, not a summary

text:
dsh-history-fold README · Nested paths: a path inside a path：The in-context index is **sampled** once it overflows, and the sampling step is capped at 64 —
so the more often a session folds, the coarser the index of its oldest spans becomes, until an
old span is reduced to "somewhere in seqs A..B". That is the part that does not scale.

So every fold now does one more thing: it writes the **unsampled** index of the range to disk
and leaves only its **path** in context.
section: Nested paths: a path inside a path

text:
dsh-history-fold README · Nested paths: a path inside a path：```
the folded message in context
  |- path -> $DSH_HOME/history-fold/index/<session>/f100-4500.md  <- full index of that range
  |            \-- path -> f20-99.md                              <- an earlier fold's full index
  |                         \-- path -> f0-19.md

Two rules make the chain hold:
section: Nested paths: a path inside a path

text:
dsh-history-fold README · Nested paths: a path inside a path：1. **Each folded message carries a machine-readable marker:**
   `[fold-index] seqs=A..B messages=N file=<tier index path>`. When that message is itself
   folded later, the marker is parsed back out — so the older span is represented by a
   **pointer**, not by a 160-character stub of an index.
2. **That line is never sampled away.** Sampling drops ordinary message lines only. Dropping a
   fold-pointer would silently *orphan* everything older than it: nothing left in context
   could reach it.
section: Nested paths: a path inside a path

text:
dsh-history-fold README · Nested paths: a path inside a path：Every tier file is self-contained on disk, and it lists the tier files of any **older** folds
that it covers (`## older tier files`). Context keeps the shortest layer; walking down the
paths reaches the raw text. Reading a tier file costs nothing until it is read — and it is
never read unless it is needed.

**Measured** on a real 1,210-turn session (surface 213,919 tokens):
section: Nested paths: a path inside a path

text:
dsh-history-fold README · Nested paths: a path inside a path：| | |
|---|---|
| folded | 614 messages / **184,709 tokens / 86.3%** |
| marker that enters context | 30,232 characters (~7.5k tokens) — about 24:1 |
| archive written | 638 KB |
| user-authored text preserved | **verbatim** |
| assistant text preserved | verbatim (the archive is a superset — it also keeps reasoning) |
section: Nested paths: a path inside a path

text:
dsh-history-fold README · Nested paths: a path inside a path：Because the archive holds the real text and the marker tells the model to search it, folded
content stays recoverable. Asked about a specific change that lived in the folded range, the
model read the archive and answered with the exact values; where content genuinely was not
in context it answered "not in context" instead of guessing.

text: dsh-history-fold README · How a recall hit is chosen：Three routes, tried in this order, and the first one that produces anything wins:
section: How a recall hit is chosen

text:
dsh-history-fold README · How a recall hit is chosen：1. **Entity map** — `recall.entityMapFile` is plain JSON: `{"key":"tiger-maus","file":"day-20261024.md","line":1709,"title":"…"}`.
   If `key` appears in the user's message (case-insensitive), that location is served. Deterministic,
   zero scoring. Extend it by editing the file; no restart needed.
2. **Rare identifiers** — a term shaped like a name (digits, dots, dashes, or an inner capital,
   length ≥ 5) that appears in at most `recall.rareMaxDf` note files. The reasoning is measured:
   `tiger-maus` lives in 2 files while "how/previous/that" live in all of them, so ranking by
   occurrence buries the only term that could locate anything.
3. **Keyword/embedding fallback** — the previous behaviour, and it is noisy by nature (2-gram
   cutting turns "有点牛逼啊" into `呲牛/牛逼/逼啊`). Set `recall.strict: true` to turn it off
   entirely: then an injection only ever happens when route 1 or 2 found something.
section: How a recall hit is chosen

text:
dsh-history-fold README · How a recall hit is chosen：Two rules apply to every route:

- **The current turn's words, not the previous turn's.** The claimed `payload.messages` are read
  first; `agent/pre-step` runs before the message reaches `session.events`.
- **Today's own note file is never served.** Reading back what was written minutes ago is
  self-reference, not memory.
section: How a recall hit is chosen

dsh-history-fold README · The table builds itself：`entity-map.auto.json` is generated from `notes.dir` and rebuilt whenever it is older than
`recall.autoMapMinutes`. The signal is narrow on purpose: a name-shaped term (digits, dots, dashes,
inner capitals, length 4-24) that the human typed **into a `##` heading**, occurring in at most
`recall.autoMapMaxDf` note files. Scanning body text instead produced 3,032 candidates, almost all
of them code symbols, file names and function names; headings are the user's own words, and that
cuts it to a couple of hundred useful ones.

section: How the two thresholds are resolved

text:
dsh-history-fold README · How the two thresholds are resolved：1. **The key is present in `config.json`.** `triggerSurfaceTokens: 300000` means 300000 — an
   explicit absolute value beats the ratio, even when the context window is perfectly
   resolvable. "Present" means present in the raw file, not in the merged config object:
   `DEFAULTS` carries these keys too, so a merged-object check would always find one and the
   ratios would never apply at all.
2. **Otherwise, if the context window resolves:** `floor(window × ratio)`. The window comes
   from `ctx.llm.resolveModelInfo(provider, model, signal).context.contextWindow` — the same
   lookup `dsh-compaction-basic` uses for its own `thresholdRatio × contextWindow`.
3. **Otherwise:** the shipped absolute default, and the log line says `default`.
section: How the two thresholds are resolved

text:
dsh-history-fold README · How the two thresholds are resolved：The ratio is what scales. A fixed 250000 can never be reached on a 128k-window model, so the
plugin silently does nothing there; on a 1M window it is only a quarter of capacity, so the
compactor gets there first.
section: How the two thresholds are resolved

text:
dsh-history-fold README · How the two thresholds are resolved：**Verified on a real DSH instance** (2026-10-12, `web` profile, a 1M-window model; the default
ratio was `0.75` at the time, which is exactly the value 0.8.2 replaced after it failed to fold
for three weeks): with a config that carries no absolute key, a turn logged `windowTokens:1000000`,
`trigger:750000`,
`target:180000`, `triggerSource:"ratio"` and
`via:"ctx.reflect.get|llm:ctx.reflect.get/agent.options"` — so `llm` was reached through
`ctx.reflect.get` and the provider/model came from `agent.options`. If none of the three lookup
paths work in your build, the line says `triggerSource: "default"` and the behaviour is exactly
what it was before this feature existed.
section: How the two thresholds are resolved

text:
dsh-history-fold README · How the two thresholds are resolved：**Calibrate the trigger against the real prompt, not against the number.** `surfaceTokens` is
DSH's own meter, and on Chinese-heavy history it under-reports what the provider actually bills by
a measured factor: on one real session, `surfaceTokens: 452,024` while the API request carried
**790,915** tokens (`cacheReadTokens + inputTokens`), a ratio of **1.737–1.769 across 35
consecutive turns**. A threshold that looks safely below the compactor's line in meter units can
therefore be far above it in real tokens.
section: How the two thresholds are resolved

text:
dsh-history-fold README · How the two thresholds are resolved：That is not hypothetical. This plugin ran `triggerSurfaceTokens: 750000` against a 1,000,000-token
window for three weeks and never folded once:
section: How the two thresholds are resolved

text:
dsh-history-fold README · How the two thresholds are resolved：| what the config looked like | what it meant |
|---|---|
| 750000 "of a 1M window", i.e. 0.75 | 1.31M **real** tokens — above the window itself |
| trigger 750000 vs. compactor at 800000 | unreachable: the compactor always fired first and rewrote the history into a model-written summary |
| the log | `idle`, `"surfaceTokens": 452024`, `"trigger": 750000` — reading, correctly, as "not needed yet" |

So: measure your own ratio before choosing a number.
section: How the two thresholds are resolved

text:
dsh-history-fold README · How the two thresholds are resolved：1. Take one `profile` line's `surfaceTokens` from `$DSH_HOME/logs/history-fold.jsonl`.
2. Take the same turn's `cacheReadTokens + inputTokens` from `$DSH_HOME/logs/vitals/vitals-*.jsonl`.
3. Divide. Keep `triggerSurfaceTokens` low enough that `trigger × ratio` stays comfortably under
   `0.8 × contextWindow`.
section: How the two thresholds are resolved

text:
dsh-history-fold README · How the two thresholds are resolved：On the 1M-window, Chinese-heavy session this project is developed against, that ratio is ~1.75, so
the working set is **`triggerSurfaceTokens: 300000` / `targetSurfaceTokens: 130000`** — ~528k real
tokens (52.8% of the window) to fold, ~234k real tokens kept. That leaves ~272k real tokens of
margin before the compactor's 800k line.

text:
dsh-history-fold README · How the two thresholds are resolved：**Since 0.8.2 the plugin checks this for you.** A trigger at or above `0.8 × window`, or at or
above the window itself, or a target at or above the trigger, writes one `threshold-warning` line
per distinct resolved pair — so the next misconfiguration is one grep away instead of three weeks
away.

dsh-history-fold README · How the two thresholds are resolved：Every profile and fold line reports what happened: `windowTokens` (the resolved window, or

|---|---|---|---|
| What replaces the history | a **model-written summary** | an **extractive index** + an archive pointer | nothing — the request is untouched |
| **Can you still quote the original** | **no** — the summary is all that survives | **yes**, verbatim, in `$DSH_HOME/history-fold/archive/` | n/a |
| Is anything invented | yes, the model writes new prose | no, the index lines are the messages' own prefixes, and no model is called | n/a |
| Recoverable | no | yes, one `rg` over the archive | n/a |
| What it changes | the surface (what the model is sent) | the surface (what the model is sent) | the **display** (long messages collapsed in the UI) |
| Trigger | `thresholdRatio × contextWindow`, 800k by default | `triggerSurfaceTokens` (or `triggerRatio × contextWindow`), calibrated against the **real** prompt size — 300000 on a Chinese-heavy 1M session; an absolute `triggerSurfaceTokens` still overrides the ratio | n/a |

text:
dsh-history-fold README · Relation to the built-in compactor, and to the other "fold"-named plugins：> **Keep the trigger below the compactor's line — in real tokens, not in meter units.**
> `dsh-compaction-basic` fires at `thresholdRatio × contextWindow` — `0.8 × 1,000,000`, so 800k —
> and keeps `0.16 × window` (160k). Its replacement is a model-written summary, which is lossy.
> Folding first is what stops that summarizer from ever firing at all. The trap is that DSH's
> `surfaceTokens` can under-report the real request by ~1.75x on Chinese text, so a trigger of
> `0.75 × window` in *meter* units is ~1.31 × window in *real* units and never fires. Measure the
> ratio (previous section), then pick the number.
section: Relation to the built-in compactor, and to the other "fold"-named plugins

text:
dsh-history-fold README · Relation to the built-in compactor, and to the other "fold"-named plugins：A plugin with `fold` in its name is often a **display** fold: it collapses a long message in
the UI so it is easier to read, and leaves the request payload exactly as it was. This plugin
is the opposite — it does not touch the UI at all, and every byte it moves is aimed at the
tokens sent on the *next* request. Decide which of the two you actually want before installing.

text:
dsh-history-fold README · Safety model：- **Inert by default.** With no config file, nothing is read, written or logged.
- **Archive before fold.** A fold commits only after its full text is on disk.
- **Balanced cuts only.** A tool call never crosses a fold boundary.
- **Balanced failures only.** A missing token meter, an unreachable session or an archive
  error all skip the fold and log it, rather than guessing.
- **Turn boundary only.** `onlyAtTurnStart` keeps a fold from ever landing mid-turn.
- **Nothing is paraphrased.** The index is extraction; only the pointer message is
  synthetic, and it is labelled `source.kind = 'plugin'`.
- **A failed index write never blocks a fold.** The archive is written first and holds every
  byte, so an index error is logged as `index-failed` and the fold proceeds; the message then
  names the raw archive instead of a tier file.

text:
dsh-history-fold README · Verified end to end：- **The in-context index is not a summary you can rely on for detail.** It was 29,937
  characters in that test, and the model did not locate a specific string inside it. Actual
  recall comes from the archive plus the notice telling the model to search it. The index
  tells the model *what exists*, not *what it said*.
- **Anything that makes DSH's token meter throw disables folding silently.** The plugin logs
  `no-meter` and skips the turn (fail open, nothing is lost), and the official compactor
  depends on the same meter. A session-sidecar pruner that emitted `placeholder` blocks was
  observed to cause exactly this; it is off by default and unrelated to the live path.

text:
dsh-history-fold README · Limitations：- Tuned and measured against DeepSeek Harness on Windows with a 1,000,000-token context
  window. The mechanism is adapter-agnostic; the shipped absolute fallbacks are not — which is
  what the ratios are for. When the window resolves, the thresholds scale with it.
- **Whether `ctx.llm` is really reachable from this plugin's context has not been confirmed
  against a live DSH.** The lookup mirrors `resolveMeter()` (direct property, then
  `ctx.reflect.get`, then the agent's own composed context) and never throws, but if no path
  works in your build the plugin logs `triggerSource: "default"` and behaves exactly as it did
  before this feature existed.
- Token counts come from DSH's `tokenMeter`. If it is unavailable the plugin does nothing —
  by design.
- Folding reduces what the model sees. The archive keeps it recoverable, but reading it back
  costs a `rg` round-trip.
- It does not (yet) coordinate with `dsh-compaction-basic`; it simply stays below its
  trigger.

text:
dsh-history-fold README · 分层索引：路径里有路径（2026-10-15）：上下文里那份索引超预算就**抽样**，而抽样步长**封顶在 64** ⇒ 折得越多，越老的那段索引越粗，
最后退化成「seqs A..B 里大概有东西」✗

所以每次折叠都多做一件事：把**没抽样的完整索引**写到磁盘，上下文里只留它的**路径** ✓

```
上下文里那条折叠消息
  |- 路径 -> $DSH_HOME/history-fold/index/<会话id>/f100-4500.md   <- 该段的完整索引（不抽样）
  |            \-- 路径 -> f20-99.md                             <- 更早那次折叠的完整索引
  |                         \-- 路径 -> f0-19.md

两条关键规则：
section: 分层索引：路径里有路径（2026-10-15）

text:
dsh-history-fold README · 分层索引：路径里有路径（2026-10-15）：1. **折叠消息里带一行机器可读的标记** ✓
   `[fold-index] seqs=A..B messages=N file=<层索引路径>`
   ⇒ 下次它自己被折掉时能被解析出来，**而不是被截成 160 字符的桩** ✓
2. **这一行永不被抽样掉** ✓（抽样只抽普通消息行）
   ⇒ 否则它盖住的那段更老的记录就成了**孤儿** —— 上下文里再也没有路能走到它 ✗

于是每一层索引都靠自己那份磁盘文件活着 ✓ 上下文里只留**最短的这一层** ✓
打开一份层索引，能看到它盖住的**更老的层索引路径**（`## older tier files`）⇒
一层层往下走，最终到原文归档 ✓

**读它不花上下文** ✓ —— 不读就等于不存在，读了才付费 ✓

> ⚠️ 与官方压缩的区别仍在这里：官方每次都**重新写一份摘要**（本机实测一个会话压了 17 次，
> 每次输入都带着上一份摘要，输出新的把它盖掉）⇒ 老信息被反复重写 ✗
> 而这里是**写盘一次 + 留路径**，落盘的东西此后不再被动过 ✓

| **折之前先归档** | 被折掉的每一条消息的**全文**写进 `$DSH_HOME/history-fold/archive/<会话id>.jsonl` ✓ |

text:
dsh-history-fold README · 折不动怎么办：第二道闸（2026-10-17 加）：正常情况折不动是不成立的 —— 触发线一过，就把能折的一段**一次折到底**（折到 `lastFoldableIdx`，
目标 180k），所以在同一轮里它不可能“折一点然后放弃”。

真正会让它空转的只有三个很窄的口子：

1. 最近还保的 `keepRecentNodes` 个节点，**它们自己就超过触发线**；
2. 存档写失败（按设计直接放弃，宁可不折也不丢）；
3. 找不到配对平衡的切点（整个可折区的工具调用/结果都配不成对）。

为了不让这三个口子把 surface 一路顶到窗口上限，加了第二道闸：
section: 折不动怎么办：第二道闸（2026-10-17 加）

text:
dsh-history-fold README · 折不动怎么办：第二道闸（2026-10-17 加）：- 下一轮如果还停在窗口的 **0.8**（`emergencyTriggerRatio`，1M 窗口 = 80 万）之上 ⇒
  说明上一次没折成 ⇒ **放宽参数再折一次**：
  - 最近节点从 `keepRecentNodes`（60）降到 `emergencyKeepRecentNodes`（12）
  - 折叠下限从 `minFoldNodes/minFoldTokens`（20 / 20000）降到 `emergencyMinFoldNodes/MinFoldTokens`（4 / 2000）
- 机制完全不变：**照样逐字归档**、**照样不切工具对**、照样只在一轮开头折 ✓
- 只是“客气程度”降低：允许少留一点最近历史 ✓
- 日志里这次折叠带 `emergency: true`，事后能分清是哪条路 ✓

> 第二道闸永远不会低于第一道：`emergency` 取 `max(绝对值, 触发线)`，
> 否则它会在同一轮里和正常折叠重复触发 ✓
